Both follow the identical recipe window.open('','_blank') -> popup-blocked guard -> document.write(<full html>) -> document.close() -> window.print(). The module-level doc block in the native file cites every source-line range it ports or adapts.

This is a faithful port of pre-existing fields, NOT the addition of new Mi/Min/Mph/Kwh/Wh-km model fields — the Phase-48 SI-canonical prohibition targets NEW struct/DB/JSON fields, not parity ports of the current web contract. The web `any` parameter types were replaced with explicit ReportDrive/ReportVehicle/ReportStats interfaces (per the no-`any` guideline and the gpx precedent), with optional/nullable members that exactly admit the source's `?.`/`??`/`!= null`/`|| 0` access.

DELIVERY (browser-only, contract rule 7): window.open (source L5, L60), document.write (L8, L63), document.close (L55, L93) and window.print (L56, L94) have NO React Native equivalent and no print/file/sharing dependency is installed in apps/native, so delivery is routed through React Native's built-in Share API (the OS share sheet) — the same native analog the already-ported gpx parity sibling uses. The web document <title> (L12 'Drive Report - ' + formatDate; L67 'TeslaSync Monthly Report') is surfaced as the share title / iOS subject / Android dialogTitle. The two exports keep their web names (generateDriveReport, generateMonthlyReport) but become async and return a structured ReportResult { title, html, delivered, action, unavailableReason? }.

The web popup-blocked early return `if (!printWindow) return` (source L6, L61) — a silent no-report outcome — maps to the EXPLICIT unavailable state required by contract rule 7: when Share throws / has no target the result is action:'unavailable' with unavailableReason (via getErrorMessage), a dismissed share sheet is action:'dismissed', and a successful share is action:'shared' / delivered:true. The built html + title are returned in every branch so the document is never lost even when delivery fails. document.close() (L55, L93) is a browser bookkeeping step with no native analog and is intentionally dropped (documented in the file header).

No DOM, window, document, Recharts, Leaflet, or web-UI symbol reaches the native output; the only platform import is react-native `Share` (contract rule 5). The only mechanical differences vs source are native formatting (prettier arrowParens:'avoid', singleQuote, trailingComma:'all', statement semicolons) and `Number.isNaN` in place of the global `isNaN` in the inlined date helpers (identical for Date.getTime()). No unit conversion is introduced — display strings (km, km/h, kWh, Wh/km, %, $) are emitted verbatim as the web does; SI display-boundary conversion is the responsibility of the future useUnits-backed pages, not this serializer.

Validation co-test added at apps/native/__tests__/WebParityReport.test.ts mirroring the established WebParityGpx.test.ts: asserts buildDriveReportHtml / buildMonthlyReportHtml structure + computed values (duration 0h 30m, average speed 85 km/h, battery used 20%, monthly 1,234 km / $78.50 / 0-fallbacks) and the Share delivery contract (shared / dismissed / explicit unavailable with unavailableReason). Locale-dependent date strings are asserted only by stable prefix. No co-located *.parity test file is added, consistent with every other web-parity/lib port.
